decisions.reason: As a low-risk complementary consumable tied to the installed base, the cleaning soap likely meets modest aspiration levels and is easy to retain within the firm's service-oriented flooring system.

The maintenance oil fits the firm's established care routine for wooden floors, and in a growing industry with some slack management would usually keep such a line unless repeated results clearly fell below aspiration.

This care product remains somewhat niche because it targets oiled floors, but it still leverages the firm's installed base and is likely to be retained while management sees no clear evidence of persistent underperformance.

The moisture-protection underlay supports installation quality and complements core floor sales, so boundedly rational management would tend to keep it absent a visible shortfall versus comparable accessories.

The high-density underlay foam is still the most vulnerable because of possible overlap and substitutability within the underlay range, but current growth and organisational slack still favor keeping it for now.

The oak parquet line is close to the firm's core capabilities, brand, and strategic direction, so it is unlikely to be dropped unless market feedback shows a clear and sustained failure to meet aspiration levels.
